what: Ending the orchestrator turn exited the Claude Code process and stopped three running subagents (recon, bars, unit tests); they were resumed from their saved transcripts. A later turn end triggered a harness validation for the missing struct-out file; a truthful provisional .terminal_claude_agent_struct_out.json was written at 01:25Z.
impact: ~30 min of wall clock lost; no data affected

what: Orchestrator printed a 2-row snippet of iteration-4 assets/pairs.json, which embeds iteration-2 behaviour rates (Qwen3-4B OR .444; Qwen3-0.6B HC .156 / OR .067). Disclosed as prereg amendment A3; pairs.json is now on the Tier-A forbidden-path list and the pair structure is defined by rule (A2).
impact: none on any definition (prereg frozen 00:49:37Z; pre-screen mechanical and audited)

what: The cumulative prereg_amendments.json had been chained twice (an append-only file cannot re-verify against its earlier digest). The two S1-amend chain records were re-issued as immutable batch files prereg_amendments_b1.json (A1-A3) and _b2.json (A4-A5); the original chain is preserved at logs/hashchain_before_reissue_0156.jsonl; src/amend.py now always writes batch files.
impact: chain verifies (3 records, digests/order/UTC/mtime all monotone); no stage after S1 existed yet

what: The strongest-tier Tier-B subagent was terminated three times by API 500 errors; the Tier-B operation was handed to a mid-tier agent working from the files already on disk (src/tierB.py, src/rowhooks.py).
core.GpuLease counted other artifacts' queued lease records ('waiting': true) as VRAM in use; patched to ignore queued reservations.

Plan-registered 'definitional' check for G2 (a near-blanket refuser should sit near zero): F1__cautious G2 = 0.53 (panel minimum; ref 0.71) holds only directionally, and F3__cautious G2 = 1.38 exceeds its ref (0.83). Both cautious arms are system-prompt refusers. Reported as a FINDING (behavioural blanket refusal via a system prompt does not collapse the three-cluster geometry at the last prompt token); the G2 code was NOT changed in response.

Build-time proposal to score confirmation checkpoints with a simplified fixed-band proxy, and to take AMS sigma from the substrate's manifest, were REJECTED (amendment A5); confirmation uses the screen's exact code.

Field-norm H (activation-patching validation, prereg patching_H, band B4, n=11 items per checkpoint): per-item Spearman between W1's projection-out effect and a REAL activation patch (last-token residual at every B4 block replaced by the mean fit-fold plain-benign activation) is +0.53 (F1__ref), -0.54 (F2__ref) and +0.40 (huihui-Qwen3-0.6B-abliterated); per fold it ranges from +0.70 to -0.49.
impact: REPORTED AS A LIMITATION OF THE WHOLE W FAMILY: the first-order directional-ablation effect does not reliably track a true patch item by item (one of three checkpoints is strongly negative), exactly the downstream-non-linearity failure mode the field has documented for first-order approximations. The registered W scalars are panel-level statistics and are reported as such; no per-item causal claim is made.

what: W2 (redundancy depth) is fold-unstable and does not transfer: on F2__ref the two cross-fit folds give k*=1 and CENSORED(7) (registered mean 4.0); on the disjoint A_c11 set (field-norm I transfer) F1__ref gives 1 vs 1, huihui-abliterated 1 vs 4, mylesgoose 4 vs 4, F2__ref 4 vs 4 with one censored fold each. Averaging a real k with the censoring code 7 produces uninterpretable intermediate values.
impact: W2 must be read through its censoring flag (10/42 rows censored), never as a plain number; the transfer check says a W2 threshold crossing is NOT a mechanism. Reported in the disclosure block.

what: Held-out compute: the substrate's arrays carry A_prompt/A_dec/r_* but no gamma, A_c11 or A_ams, so AMS sigma, A1_slope and BL1_truelogit are not computable from them. src/bars_partial.py adds a shim (gamma=ones, gamma-dependent bars forced to NaN) and src/confirm_harvest_all.py runs OUR OWN 27-file harvest + registered Tier-B battery per Hub checkpoint. The 8 in-house PB__ernie03b__* arms cannot be rebuilt (no Hub repo), so they are Tier-A + BL1 only.
impact: per-row coverage is reported; nothing is imputed

what: External harvest failed for 3 architectures on the first pass (GPT-NeoX/Bloom block discovery, an attention-backend error needing eager, and a tokenizer with no pad token). A fix + re-run was delegated with a 04:45Z stop.
impact: any checkpoint still failing is scored Tier-A-only from the substrate's arrays and reported as such

what: On the held-out panel the W-family normaliser `gap` (the harmful-vs-benign r_late separation on the scoring fold) is near-degenerate for base models with no refusal behaviour: pythia-410m gap 1.28 and Pleias-1.2b 2.63 (plain_DiM 0.96 and 0.50 Cohen's d) versus a screen-panel median plain_DiM of 3.2, which inflates W1 to -4.8 and +20.3 against a screen-panel range of roughly -0.1..1.5. The prereg guards W3/G2/A3 denominators but not `gap`.
impact: the REGISTERED primary keeps every landed row; a DISCLOSED post-hoc sensitivity that drops rows with |plain_DiM| < 1.0 is reported beside it (src/confirm_cluster_sensitivity.py -> non_degenerate_readout_sensitivity), together with the affected tags

what: The released ams-scanner CLI validation subset (3 panel models at batch 1 and 8) was NOT RUN: the delegated CPU run stalled repairing the .venv_ams torch install and was abandoned rather than allowed to contend with the GPU pipeline. results/ams_cli_validation.json does not exist.
impact: The AMS bar in this artifact is the labelled reimplementation (src/reuse/ams_reimpl.py, batch 1 from A_ams) plus a batch-8 right-padding EMULATION computed in the Tier-B pass; the released-package cross-check is cited from iteration 4 (results/ams_validation.json there: reimpl agrees with the CLI within 0.01% at batch 1; at batch 8 the CLI's padding=True-without-padding_side bug moves Falcon3 by 5.3 sigma). Disclosed rather than presented as our own validation.
